issuer: the Secretary to the Department of Transport and Planning (VicRoads)
note: Read 2026-10-30 from the Victorian Legislation site's authorised Word versions (converted to text, saved beside them). The Road Safety Act 1986 (version 237) grants a driver licence to a person over the age of 18 (s 19(1)) and sets its fee in fee units: 5.59 for a 3-year licence, 7.45 for a 4-year one and 19.15 for a 10-year one (s 21A). Until 2026-10-30 the file held the 10-year term, its fee null. From 2026-10-30 it holds two terms, 3 years at 5.59 fee units and 10 years at 19.15, each worth the fee unit's value on the day paid (the game holds Victoria's fee unit, VFU). The 3-year term is read as a full licence's from reg 105, which makes a '3 year full driver licence' free to a good probationary driver the first time; the 4-year licence of s 21A(1)(b) is read as the P2 probationary licence granted for 4 years under reg 51(5), not a full licence's term, and isn't held. Neither text says in so many words that the holder chooses between 3 and 10 years: that the two are terms the holder chooses among is a reading. The Road Safety (Drivers) Regulations 2019 (version 021, in force 30 September 2026): a first licence under 21 is a P1 probationary licence for one year (reg 50), followed by a P2 probationary licence for 3 years (reg 52(5)), and a full licence is granted when the probationary period ends (reg 49(2)): a full licence is kept from 22. The fee unit's dollar value (set each financial year by the Treasurer under the Monetary Units Act 2004) wasn't read with the licence, and VicRoads' fee pages refused the request behind a Cloudflare check, so until 2026-10-30 the fee stood null. Not held: the free first probationary licence and first 3-year full licence (regs 104A and 105), the 25% discount on a good driver's renewal (reg 104B), and the shorter term the Secretary may give a holder of 75 or older (s 19(4A)). Victoria's Proof of Age card isn't held. The lead (2026-10-30) held the ten-year licence alone at its 19.15 fee units: no saved text says the holder chooses between three and ten years (as with the ACT, whose regulation has the authority set the period), so the three-year licence at 5.59 fee units is in the note only; until then the fee stood null.

sources.said: The Secretary may, on the application of a person over the age of 18 years, grant a driver licence ... (c) in the case of a 10 year licence—19·15 fee units. ... (1) Subject to the regulations, the fees payable for the grant or renewal of a driver licence are as follows— ... (a) in the case of a 3 year licence—5·59 fee units; ... (b) in the case of a 4 year licence—7·45 fee units; ... the Secretary may renew a driver licence held by a person who is 75 years of age or over for a shorter term than the term that usually applies to a person who is less than 75 years of age.
